ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a relatively thick and uniform tree branch, which as a whole is in an arc shape arching upward, with the middle position the highest; point A is on the lower slope section on the right side, point B is on the lower slope section on the left side, and the small bird slowly crawls along the tree branch from A on the right side toward B on the left side. Therefore, when moving leftward from A, the small bird first approaches the top of the arch along the right-side slope, and the tangent to the tree branch gradually approaches horizontal; after passing over the top of the arch, it then moves toward B along the left-side slope, and the tangent to the tree branch again gradually becomes inclined. Then reason: The small bird moves slowly, so it can approximately be regarded as being in force equilibrium at every position. The small bird is subject to gravity mg, the elastic force N of the tree branch, and friction along the direction of the tree branch. Decompose gravity into the two directions perpendicular to the tree branch and along the tree branch; the elastic force of the tree branch on the small bird is equal to the component of gravity in the direction perpendicular to the tree branch. If the angle between the tangent to the tree branch and the horizontal direction is θ, then the magnitude of the perpendicular component is N = mg cosθ. When the small bird goes from A to the top of the arch, θ gradually decreases to 0, and cosθ increases, so the elastic force increases; when it goes from the top of the arch to B, θ again gradually increases, and cosθ decreases, so the elastic force decreases. Final answer: The elastic force of the tree branch on the small bird first increases and then decreases.
